papers.title: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome outbreak linked to cruise ship travel in April-May 2026.
papers.abstract: In April 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. ANDV genome sequences were obtained for 10 of the 13 identified cases during a cross-country investigation established to share initial raw data for joint analysis with reciprocal quality control. The genomic data, symptom onsets, and plausible contact patterns strongly support a tightly linked outbreak cluster compatible with a single or very few zoonotic spillover events prior to embarkment followed by human-to-human transmission onboard. papers.title: Immunogenicity of Hantavirus and evaluation of vaccine protective efficacy: A comparative neutralizing antibody study of vaccine strains and representative epidemic strains from selected provinces in China.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantavirus (HV) remains a significant public health burden in the world. HFRS bivalent inactivated vaccine (HFRSbiv) with Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV) strains isolated 20 years ago have been used in key HFRS endemic provinces in China for HFRS prevention. After decades of effective implementation of comprehensive prevention and control measures, HFRS has entered a stage of epidemic fluctuation at low-level in China. However, the continuous transmission of the virus among rodent host animals may lead to dynamic changes in genetic diversity and immunogenicity of the virus, which may affect the pathogenic mechanism of the virus and the protective effect of vaccines. It is necessary to carry out timely monitoring and evaluation of the immunogenicity of HV. METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: A panel of sera was established by screening serum samples from HFRS patients at convalescent phase and individuals who had received standardized immunization with HFRSbiv. Neutralizing antibody titers against HTNV vaccine strain 84FLi, SEOV vaccine strain L99, and three representative epidemic strains from different genotypes (HTNV: SX26, SEOV: LN03 and FJ-17) were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay-based microneutralization test (MN-ELISA). HV-neutralizing antibodies were detected from all the selected serum samples. Among HFRS patients, 47.92% (23/48) were identified as HTNV infection, 27.08% (13/48) were with SEOV infection, and 25% (12/48) were untypable. There is a significant difference in the titers of neutralizing antibodies against vaccine strains and epidemic strains detected in the serum samples. For HTNV, both patient and vaccinee sera exhibited significantly higher geometric mean titer (GMT) against vaccine strain 84FLi than against epidemic strain SX26 (1:386.08 vs. 1:223.04, P < 0.001; 1:137.94 vs. 1:110.37, P < 0.05, respectively). For SEOV, patient sera showed significantly lower GMT against vaccine strain L99 than against epidemic strain LN03 (1:177.02 vs. 1:297.71, P < 0.01), and vaccinee sera showed significantly lower GMT against L99 than against epidemic strain FJ-17 (1:97.52 vs. 1:243.71, P < 0.001). Significant immunogenicity heterogeneity was observed between SEOV epidemic strains LN03 and FJ-17. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: The genetic diversity and immunogenicity of HV, which causes HFRS, have certain geographical regional characteristics. The levels of cross neutralizing antibodies induced by infection of HV from different genotypes may vary significantly, but still provide sufficient cross protection. The HFRSbiv currently used in China could induce broad neutralizing antibody, the cross-protective efficacy might vary against different circulating strains and genotypes. It is of great significance to strengthen the monitoring of genetic characteristics of regional specific circulating viral strains, regularly evaluate the matching degree between vaccine protection effectiveness and epidemic strains, predict and evaluate the transmission and pathogenic risks of HV, and timely optimize HFRS prevention and control strategies and measures.

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 的免疫原性和 疫苗 保护功效的评估:疫苗 株与中国部分省份代表性流行株的中和抗体比较研究。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantavirus (HV) remains a significant public health burden in the world. HFRS bivalent inactivated vaccine (HFRSbiv) with Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV) strains isolated 20 years ago have been used in key HFRS endemic provinces in China for HFRS prevention. After decades of effective implementation of comprehensive prevention and control measures, HFRS has entered a stage of epidemic fluctuation at low-level in China. However, the continuous transmission of the virus among rodent host animals may lead to dynamic changes in genetic diversity and immunogenicity of the virus, which may affect the pathogenic mechanism of the virus and the protective effect of vaccines. It is necessary to carry out timely monitoring and evaluation of the immunogenicity of HV. METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: A panel of sera was established by screening serum samples from HFRS patients at convalescent phase and individuals who had received standardized immunization with HFRSbiv. Neutralizing antibody titers against HTNV vaccine strain 84FLi, SEOV vaccine strain L99, and three representative epidemic strains from different genotypes (HTNV: SX26, SEOV: LN03 and FJ-17) were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay-based microneutralization test (MN-ELISA). HV-neutralizing antibodies were detected from all the selected serum samples. Among HFRS patients, 47.92% (23/48) were identified as HTNV infection, 27.08% (13/48) were with SEOV infection, and 25% (12/48) were untypable. There is a significant difference in the titers of neutralizing antibodies against vaccine strains and epidemic strains detected in the serum samples. For HTNV, both patient and vaccinee sera exhibited significantly higher geometric mean titer (GMT) against vaccine strain 84FLi than against epidemic strain SX26 (1:386.08 vs. 1:223.04, P < 0.001; 1:137.94 vs. 1:110.37, P < 0.05, respectively). For SEOV, patient sera showed significantly lower GMT against vaccine strain L99 than against epidemic strain LN03 (1:177.02 vs. 1:297.71, P < 0.01), and vaccinee sera showed significantly lower GMT against L99 than against epidemic strain FJ-17 (1:97.52 vs. 1:243.71, P < 0.001). Significant immunogenicity heterogeneity was observed between SEOV epidemic strains LN03 and FJ-17. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: The genetic diversity and immunogenicity of HV, which causes HFRS, have certain geographical regional characteristics. The levels of cross neutralizing antibodies induced by infection of HV from different genotypes may vary significantly, but still provide sufficient cross protection. The HFRSbiv currently used in China could induce broad neutralizing antibody, the cross-protective efficacy might vary against different circulating strains and genotypes. It is of great significance to strengthen the monitoring of genetic characteristics of regional specific circulating viral strains, regularly evaluate the matching degree between vaccine protection effectiveness and epidemic strains, predict and evaluate the transmission and pathogenic risks of HV, and timely optimize HFRS prevention and control strategies and measures.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:由汉坦病毒(HV) 引起的 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 仍然是世界上重大的公共卫生负担。20年前分离出的含有汉坦病毒(HTNV)和汉城病毒(SEOV)毒株的HFRS二价灭活疫苗(HFRSbiv)已在中国HFRS重点流行省份用于预防HFRS。经过几十年的综合防控措施的有效实施,我国HFRS已进入疫情低水平波动阶段。然而,该病毒在啮齿动物宿主动物中的持续传播可能会导致病毒遗传多样性和免疫原性的动态变化,从而可能影响病毒的致病机制和疫苗的保护作用。有必要及时开展HV免疫原性监测和评估。方法学/主要发现:通过筛选恢复期 HFRS 患者和接受 HFRSbiv 标准化免疫的个体的血清样本,建立了一组血清。使用基于酶联免疫吸附测定的微中和试验(MN-ELISA)测量了针对 HTNV 疫苗 株 84FLi、SEOV 疫苗 株 L99 和来自不同基因型的三种代表性流行株(HTNV:SX26、SEOV:LN03 和 FJ-17)的中和抗体滴度。从所有选定的血清样本中均检测到 HV 中和抗体。HFRS患者中,47.92%(23/48)被诊断为HTNV感染,27.08%(13/48)被诊断为SEOV感染,25%(12/48)未被分型。血清样本中检测到的疫苗株与流行株的中和抗体滴度存在显着差异。对于 HTNV,患者和疫苗接种者血清对 疫苗 84FLi 株的几何平均滴度 (GMT) 均显着高于流行株 SX26(分别为 1:386.08 vs. 1:223.04,P < 0.001;1:137.94 vs. 1:110.37,P < 0.05)。对于SEOV,患者血清针对疫苗毒株L99的GMT显着低于针对流行毒株LN03的GMT(1:177.02 vs. 1:297.71,P < 0.01),并且接种者血清针对L99的GMT显示显着低于针对流行毒株FJ-17的GMT(1:97.52 vs. 1:243.71,P < 0.01)。0.001)。SEOV 流行毒株 LN03 和 FJ-17 之间观察到显着的免疫原性异质性。结论/意义:导致 HFRS 的 HV 的遗传多样性和免疫原性具有一定的地理区域特征。不同基因型 HV 感染诱导的交叉中和抗体水平可能差异很大,但仍能提供足够的交叉保护。目前国内使用的HFRSbiv可诱导广泛的中和抗体,针对不同的流行毒株和基因型,交叉保护效果可能有所不同。加强地区特定流行病毒株遗传特征监测,定期评估疫苗防护效果与流行毒株的匹配程度,预测评估疫苗和HV致病风险,及时优化HFRS防控策略和措施具有重要意义。

papers.title: The Potential Risk Factors of Hantavirus Transmission to Humans from Infected Rodents in Malaysia
papers.abstract: Zoonotic hantavirus is a negative single-stranded RNA virus from the family Bunyaviridae which is known to cause two significant rodent-borne diseases in humans namely hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), affecting about 30 000 people worldwide each year. HFRS is a disease found endemically in Asia and Europe with case fatality rates varying from <1% to 12%, while HPS which has a higher mortality rate of approximately 40% occurs within the American continent. Many countries in Southeast Asia unaware the public health implication of Hantavirus infection despite favorable ecological conditions include rich rodent species diversity, urbanisation and high human-wildlife interface that serve as ecological condition that could support the virus persistence and transmission.Since humans serve as spillover hosts who are infected largely by inhalation of infected rodents’ excreta, it is crucial to fill in the research gap by identifying the risk factors for human hantavirus infection. This paper provides a review of the potential risk factors associated with hantavirus transmission to humans from infected rodents in Malaysia focusing on behavioral, occupational, urban, and environmental. Other pieces of knowledge such as hantavirus virological properties, the geographical distribution with its respective role as a reservoir, clinical features, and diagnostic challenges, particularly its propensity to be misclassified due to mimic symptom with dengue and leptospirosis. To effectively mitigate transmission, Malaysia must transition from a fragmented surveillance model to a proactive, integrated One Health framework that bridges the inter-governmental agencies through a unified data-sharing platform to monitor active viral strains and prevent localised spillover outbreaks.

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 传播 对马来西亚受感染啮齿动物的潜在风险因素
papers.source_body_en: Zoonotic hantavirus is a negative single-stranded RNA virus from the family Bunyaviridae which is known to cause two significant rodent-borne diseases in humans namely hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), affecting about 30 000 people worldwide each year. HFRS is a disease found endemically in Asia and Europe with case fatality rates varying from <1% to 12%, while HPS which has a higher mortality rate of approximately 40% occurs within the American continent. Many countries in Southeast Asia unaware the public health implication of Hantavirus infection despite favorable ecological conditions include rich rodent species diversity, urbanisation and high human-wildlife interface that serve as ecological condition that could support the virus persistence and transmission.Since humans serve as spillover hosts who are infected largely by inhalation of infected rodents’ excreta, it is crucial to fill in the research gap by identifying the risk factors for human hantavirus infection. This paper provides a review of the potential risk factors associated with hantavirus transmission to humans from infected rodents in Malaysia focusing on behavioral, occupational, urban, and environmental. Other pieces of knowledge such as hantavirus virological properties, the geographical distribution with its respective role as a reservoir, clinical features, and diagnostic challenges, particularly its propensity to be misclassified due to mimic symptom with dengue and leptospirosis. To effectively mitigate transmission, Malaysia must transition from a fragmented surveillance model to a proactive, integrated One Health framework that bridges the inter-governmental agencies through a unified data-sharing platform to monitor active viral strains and prevent localised spillover outbreaks.

papers.title: Molecular evolution of Andes virus lineages leading to recent human outbreaks
papers.abstract: Abstract Andes virus (ANDV) is exceptional among hantaviruses in its capacity for person-to-person transmission, but whether outbreaks reflect recent viral adaptation or emergence of pre-existing reservoir lineages remains unclear. We generated paired blood- and nasal-derived genomes from the MV Hondius outbreak and integrated them with a segment-linked collection of human- and rodent-derived ANDV sequences, including incomplete genomes. We developed a linkage-informed missing-segment framework that preserves isolate identity, sampling time, and cross-segment placement without imputing nucleotide states, enabling sensitivity analyses of patchy segment coverage. Across five human outbreaks, dated phylogenies placed outbreak lineages independently within geographically structured reservoir diversity, with closest sampled ancestry predating detection. Time-dependent-rate analyses indicated a deeper reservoir-associated history, while mutation reconstruction, selection tests, branch-rate comparisons, and structural mapping found no recurrent adaptive transition preceding human transmission. MV Hondius samples showed minimal consensus-level diversification. These results shift attention from repeated recent adaptation toward deeper lineage properties and ecological opportunity.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 摘要安第斯病毒(ANDV) 在汉坦病毒中因其具有人传人 传播 的能力而显得特殊,但 暴发 是否反映了最近的病毒适应或预先存在的 储存宿主 谱系的出现仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 提供的证据没有明确说明研究设计、设置或研究人群。
elements_zh.methods: 我们开发了一个连锁通知的缺失片段框架,该框架可以保留分离物身份、采样时间和跨片段放置,而无需估算核苷酸状态,从而能够对不完整片段覆盖进行敏感性分析。
elements_zh.main_results: MV Hondius 样本表现出最小的共识水平多样化。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 时间依赖性速率分析表明了更深层次的 储存宿主 相关历史,而 突变 重建、选择测试、分支速率比较和结构映射发现人类 传播 之前没有经常性的适应性转变。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果将人们的注意力从近期的反复适应转向更深层次的谱系特性和生态机会。

papers.title_zh: 安第斯山脉病毒谱系的分子 进化 导致最近的人类 暴发
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Andes virus (ANDV) is exceptional among hantaviruses in its capacity for person-to-person transmission, but whether outbreaks reflect recent viral adaptation or emergence of pre-existing reservoir lineages remains unclear. We generated paired blood- and nasal-derived genomes from the MV Hondius outbreak and integrated them with a segment-linked collection of human- and rodent-derived ANDV sequences, including incomplete genomes. We developed a linkage-informed missing-segment framework that preserves isolate identity, sampling time, and cross-segment placement without imputing nucleotide states, enabling sensitivity analyses of patchy segment coverage. Across five human outbreaks, dated phylogenies placed outbreak lineages independently within geographically structured reservoir diversity, with closest sampled ancestry predating detection. Time-dependent-rate analyses indicated a deeper reservoir-associated history, while mutation reconstruction, selection tests, branch-rate comparisons, and structural mapping found no recurrent adaptive transition preceding human transmission. MV Hondius samples showed minimal consensus-level diversification. These results shift attention from repeated recent adaptation toward deeper lineage properties and ecological opportunity.

papers.title: Long-term local circulation of an Andes virus lineage in northern Patagonia is linked to the M/V Hondius outbreak.
papers.abstract: In 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. Analyses revealed an unexpected relationship to an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Retrospective investigation clarified the 2018 outbreak could involve person-to-person transmission and a common ANDV lineage spanned HPS cases from 2018 to 2025 in a geographically defined area in northern Patagonia, without widespread community transmission of ANDV. Route reconstruction for the index cases in the cruise ship outbreak identified geographically plausible exposures to viruses of this lineage in Argentina, but their timing was inconsistent with the expected ANDV incubation period. The infection source for the cruise ship outbreak cannot be resolved with current information, highlighting the need to expand viral surveillance in the ANDV endemic region.
authors: International Consortium Investigating the M/V Hondius Outbreak

papers.title: An NCG mouse model of Hantaan virus reveals systemic infection and organ-specific cellular tropism.
papers.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantaan virus (HTNV) is primarily endemic across Eurasia, posing a severe threat of renal failure and mortality. The mechanisms of HTNV infection remain poorly understood, largely due to the lack of susceptible animal models. In this study, we established a systemic HTNV infection mouse model using highly immunodeficient NCG mice. Following viral inoculation, we assessed viral loads via quantitative RT-PCR and mapped cellular tropism and co-localization of HTNV with potential receptors using immunofluorescence staining. While histopathological lesions were subclinical, HTNV-infected NCG mice exhibited robust viremia and sustained viral replication across multiple organs, including the kidney, lung, spleen, reproductive organs, and liver. HTNV exhibited distinct organ-specific cellular tropism in vivo, predominantly targeting fibroblasts and interstitial cells of the renal collecting duct in the kidney, alveolar epithelial cells and macrophages in the lung, and broadly infecting multiple cell populations in the brain and ovary. Co-localization analyses indicated HTNV infection might be associated with distinct entry receptors across target organs: potentially ITGB1 and gC1qR in specific renal cells, and ITGB1 and ITGB2 in pulmonary AT1 cells and macrophages, respectively. These findings demonstrate that NCG mouse is a valuable in vivo model for studying HTNV replication and systemic dissemination.

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒的 NCG 小鼠模型揭示了全身感染和器官特异性细胞向性。
papers.source_body_en: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantaan virus (HTNV) is primarily endemic across Eurasia, posing a severe threat of renal failure and mortality. The mechanisms of HTNV infection remain poorly understood, largely due to the lack of susceptible animal models. In this study, we established a systemic HTNV infection mouse model using highly immunodeficient NCG mice. Following viral inoculation, we assessed viral loads via quantitative RT-PCR and mapped cellular tropism and co-localization of HTNV with potential receptors using immunofluorescence staining. While histopathological lesions were subclinical, HTNV-infected NCG mice exhibited robust viremia and sustained viral replication across multiple organs, including the kidney, lung, spleen, reproductive organs, and liver. HTNV exhibited distinct organ-specific cellular tropism in vivo, predominantly targeting fibroblasts and interstitial cells of the renal collecting duct in the kidney, alveolar epithelial cells and macrophages in the lung, and broadly infecting multiple cell populations in the brain and ovary. Co-localization analyses indicated HTNV infection might be associated with distinct entry receptors across target organs: potentially ITGB1 and gC1qR in specific renal cells, and ITGB1 and ITGB2 in pulmonary AT1 cells and macrophages, respectively. These findings demonstrate that NCG mouse is a valuable in vivo model for studying HTNV replication and systemic dissemination.
papers.abstract_zh: 由汉滩病毒 (HTNV) 引起的 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 主要在欧亚大陆流行,对肾衰竭和 死亡率 构成严重威胁。HTNV 感染的机制仍然知之甚少,很大程度上是由于缺乏易感动物模型。在这项研究中,我们使用高度免疫缺陷的NCG小鼠建立了系统性HTNV感染小鼠模型。病毒接种后,我们通过定量 RT-PCR 评估病毒载量,并使用免疫荧光染色绘制 HTNV 的细胞趋向性和与潜在受体的共定位。虽然组织病理学病变是亚临床的,但感染 HTNV 的 NCG 小鼠表现出强烈的病毒血症,并在多个器官(包括肾、肺、脾、生殖器官和肝脏)中持续病毒复制。HTNV在体内表现出独特的器官特异性细胞趋向性,主要针对肾脏中肾集合管的成纤维细胞和间质细胞,肺中的肺泡上皮细胞和巨噬细胞,并广泛感染大脑和卵巢中的多个细胞群。共定位分析表明,HTNV 感染可能与靶器官中不同的进入受体相关:特定肾细胞中可能存在 ITGB1 和 gC1qR,肺 AT1 细胞和巨噬细胞中分别存在 ITGB1 和 ITGB2。这些发现表明,NCG 小鼠是研究 HTNV 复制和系统传播的有价值的体内模型。

papers.title: Persistent leukopenia masks hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome.
papers.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) typically comes with fever, facial flushing, rash, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, coagulopathy and leukocytosis. However, atypical manifestations may obscure diagnosis. A 30-year-old man with rodent exposure had high fever, thrombocytopenia, and persistent leukopenia, without overt renal dysfunction despite mild renal involvement in the form of proteinuria. Hantaan virus was confirmed by serology and RT-PCR. The patient recovered following ribavirin and supportive management. This case highlights that in HFRS-endemic regions, hantavirus infection should be suspected among patients with unexplained fever, thrombocytopenia, and persistent leukopenia rather than the typical leukocytosis, even without overt renal dysfunction.

papers.title: Rat Hepatitis E Virus and Seoul Hantavirus in Pet Rats, Germany
papers.abstract: Pet rats represent a reservoir of multiple zoonotic pathogens. We demonstrated that pet rats, previously confirmed to be Seoul orthohantavirus–infected and involved in human infections in Germany, were concurrently infected with rat hepatitis E virus. The high degree of rat hepatitis E virus sequence identity suggests a single incursion event.

papers.title: Assessing the performance of time series prediction models for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome across different high-risk areas in Shaanxi Province, China
papers.abstract: Background Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a climate-sensitive disease. Existing forecasting models often overlook prefecture-level variations and environmental drivers. This study compares time series models incorporating environmental factors for prefecture-level HFRS prediction. Methods Monthly HFRS case counts and 14 environmental factors were collected from 2005 to 2023 in four typical prefecture-level cities, including Xi'an, Baoji, Xianyang, and Weinan. Core factors were determined via stepwise screening. We developed four time series models: univariate seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (SARIMA) and long short-term memory (LSTM), alongside their multivariate counterparts with exogenous variables (SARIMAX and LSTMX). Specifically, multivariate models incorporated screened environmental drivers, whereas univariate models relied solely on historical epidemic data. Model robustness was further assessed by rolling-origin validation across three test years (2021−2023), in which the entire modeling pipeline was re-executed within each training window, and the sensitivity of LSTMX performance to the covariate-selection strategy was quantified. Results The predictive value of environmental covariates for HFRS forecasting varied by city and evaluation context. In Xi'an and Baoji, the multivariate LSTMX model showed lower forecasting errors (Xi'an: R 2 = 0.976, RMSE decreased from 69.246 to 17.782; Baoji: R 2 = 0.950, RMSE decreased from 6.694 to 2.805). Conversely, in Xianyang and Weinan, univariate SARIMA yielded lower errors (R 2 = 0.940 and 0.889, respectively), and incorporating covariates did not reduce forecasting errors. Rolling-origin validation across 2021–2023 yielded a consistent ranking: LSTMX had the lowest mean RMSE in Xi'an and Baoji, whereas univariate models had lower errors in Xianyang and Weinan. Sensitivity analyses indicated that the screened covariate set was the only strategy that never caused a severe loss of accuracy, whereas including all 14 environmental variables did not reduce errors in Xianyang and Weinan. Pairwise model differences were not statistically significant after Holm correction, and the city ranking changed when the models were refitted on the monthly crude incidence-rate scale; the rankings are therefore reported descriptively and are not interpreted as evidence of regional differences in environmental effects. Conclusions No single forecasting configuration was uniformly optimal across cities: LSTMX with lagged environmental factors yielded the lowest errors in Xi'an and Baoji, whereas univariate models yielded lower errors in Xianyang and Weinan; however, these pairwise differences did not reach statistical significance after Holm correction and changed under the incidence-rate scale. When extending these models to new settings, both univariate and covariate-enhanced configurations should be compared.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 是一种气候敏感疾病。现有的预测模型常常忽视地级市的变化和环境驱动因素。本研究比较了纳入环境因素的地市级 HFRS 预测的时间序列模型。方法收集西安、宝鸡、咸阳、渭南4个典型地级市2005—2023年每月HFRS病例数和14个环境因素。通过逐步筛选确定核心因素。我们开发了四种时间序列模型:单变量季节性自回归积分移动平均线 (SARIMA) 和长短期记忆 (LSTM),以及具有外生变量的多元对应模型(SARIMAX 和 LSTMX)。具体来说,多变量模型纳入了筛选的环境驱动因素,而单变量模型仅依赖于历史流行病数据。通过三个测试年(2021−2023)的滚动源验证进一步评估了模型的稳健性,其中在每个训练窗口内重新执行整个建模流程,并量化了 LSTMX 性能对协变量选择策略的敏感性。结果 HFRS 预测的环境协变量的预测值因城市和评估背景而异。在西安和宝鸡,多元LSTMX模型显示出较低的预测误差(西安:R 2 = 0.976,RMSE从69.246下降到17.782;宝鸡:R 2 = 0.950,RMSE从6.694下降到2.805)。相反,在咸阳和渭南,单变量 SARIMA 产生的误差较低(R 2 分别 = 0.940 和 0.889),并且纳入协变量并没有减少预测误差。2021-2023 年的滚动原点验证得出了一致的排名:LSTMX 在西安和宝鸡的平均 RMSE 最低,而单变量模型在咸阳和渭南的误差较低。敏感性分析表明,筛选的协变量集是唯一不会造成准确性严重损失的策略,而包括所有 14 个环境变量并没有减少咸阳和渭南的误差。Holm修正后两两模型差异不具有统计学意义,模型在月度粗发病率率量表上重新拟合后城市排名发生变化;因此,排名是描述性报告的,并不被解释为环境影响区域差异的证据。结论 没有单一的预测配置在各个城市中都是一致最优的:具有滞后环境因素的 LSTMX 在西安和宝鸡产生的误差最低,而单变量模型在咸阳和渭南产生的误差较低;然而,这些成对差异在 Holm 校正后并未达到统计学显着性,并且在 发病率 速率量表下发生了变化。将这些模型扩展到新设置时,应比较单变量和协变量增强配置。

papers.full_text: BackgroundHemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a zoonotic disease caused by orthohantaviruses, characterized by fever, thrombocytopenia, renal impairment, and capillary leak syndrome. Its atypical presentations can closely mimic acute pancreatitis (AP), posing substantial diagnostic challenges.Case presentationA 33-year-old man presented with fever, vomiting, and watery diarrhea. Initial computed tomography (CT) revealed peripancreatic and perirenal exudation suggestive of severe acute pancreatitis. He already had profound thrombocytopenia on admission (nadir 29 × 109/L), progressive renal impairment, hematuria, and proteinuria, without typical pancreatitis risk factors or elevated pancreatic enzymes. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated progressive retroperitoneal exudation with relatively mild pancreatic parenchymal changes and newly developed bilateral pleural effusion. Whole-blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected high-copy Seoul orthohantavirus, with concurrent hepatitis B virus. The patient recovered fully with supportive care, intravenous immunoglobulin, and symptomatic treatment; pre-discharge ultrasound showed normal pancreatic morphology.ConclusionSeoul orthohantavirus infection can closely mimic severe acute pancreatitis clinically and radiologically. Disproportionate thrombocytopenia, renal involvement, and progressive retroperitoneal exudation with preserved pancreatic parenchyma are key diagnostic clues, and mNGS enables early definitive pathogen confirmation, facilitating appropriate management. Laboratory and imaging findingsInitial laboratory investigations showed a mixed acid-base disturbance, characterized by respiratory alkalosis with normal anion-gap (AnGap 2-10 mmol/L),hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and liver function injury. The most striking abnormality was profound thrombocytopenia (29 × 109/L); urinalysis revealed hematuria and proteinuria.Table 2 was revised to add serum amylase, lipase, serum triglyceride, serum urea, serum creatinine, sodium, potassium, hemoglobin values. Reticulocyte count was not tested in clinical practice; hemoglobin levels over serial time-points are presented to evaluate for bone-marrow suppression. Urine sediment examination did not demonstrate granular or hyaline casts. Serial urine output was prospectively recorded as part of intensive care monitoring; overall urine output remained adequate throughout hospitalization without anuria or oliguric renal failure. Mild anemia was observed (minimum hemoglobin 127 g/L).Serial changes in leukocytes, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, neutrophil and lymphocyte percentages, transaminases, platelets, albumin, and coagulation parameters are summarized in Table 2. The dynamic clinical, laboratory, imaging, and management course across hospitalization is summarized in the diagnostic timeline (Table 1).Table 1Diagnostic timeline.Time pointClinical manifestationsKey laboratory findingsImaging & pathogen testClinical management & decision-makingOne week before admissionLow-grade intermittent fever, lumbago; mild fatty liver; no pancreatic swelling or peripancreatic fluidDischarged; outpatient follow-up scheduled for liver function and HBV monitoring DiscussionThis case highlights a diagnostically challenging presentation in which Seoul orthohantavirus infection clinically and radiologically mimicked severe acute pancreatitis, underscoring the need to consider HFRS in the differential diagnosis of unexplained pancreatitis-like presentations (1). Acute pancreatitis is a recognized but rare complication of HFRS (2, 6), and its distinction from hantavirus-induced pancreatic involvement is notoriously difficult because of overlapping clinical and imaging features (9). The present case further illustrates that peripancreatic exudation and retroperitoneal fluid—hallmark findings of severe acute pancreatitis—can also result from the profound systemic capillary leakage and retroperitoneal edema characteristic of hantavirus infection (4, 5). In this context, marked thrombocytopenia, renal impairment with hematuria and proteinuria, and the absence of typical pancreatitis risk factors constituted pivotal clues that prompted consideration of an alternative etiology (9). Moreover, the normal pancreatic enzyme levels observed here demonstrate that biochemical markers alone cannot reliably exclude HFRS in suspected pancreatitis (10).It should be acknowledged that severe acute pancreatitis itself may produce thrombocytopenia and renal dysfunction secondary to systemic inflammation. However, several features argued against primary acute pancreatitis in this patient: thrombocytopenia was already present at initial presentation as a critical-value finding before any expected inflammatory peak of pancreatitis; renal injury was accompanied by prominent urinary findings (hematuria and proteinuria) typical for hantavirus-mediated tubular injury rather than purely pre-renal renal impairment secondary to pancreatitis-related hypovolemia; and serum amylase/lipase remained within normal reference ranges throughout admission despite extensive peripancreatic exudates on CT imaging.The dynamic imaging feature observed in this case—progressive retroperitoneal exudation on contrast-enhanced CT accompanied by relatively mild pancreatic parenchymal changes—merits particular attention in the differential diagnosis of hantavirus infection presenting with abdominal manifestations. While AP is a recognized complication of HFRS, the typical CT findings in such cases commonly include pancreatic enlargement, peripancreatic edema, and occasionally necrosis or hemorrhage (4). However, extensive retroperitoneal involvement with a relatively preserved pancreatic gland reflects the underlying pathophysiological hallmark of hantavirus infection—virus-induced increased microvascular permeability leading to fluid extravasation into the retroperitoneal space. Indeed, the retroperitoneum has been identified as a major site of vascular leak in HFRS (11), and established evidence indicates that hantavirus elicits a robust inflammatory cascade with cytokine release and endothelial dysfunction that can produce extensive retroperitoneal fluid accumulation even in the absence of true pancreatic necrosis (12, 13). Prior case reports of HFRS mimicking acute pancreatitis have generally relied on single-time-point scans and could not capture this evolving radiological signature (7). Recognition of this distinctive pattern is of substantial practical importance, particularly in endemic regions (14, 15). From a clinical standpoint, progressive retroperitoneal exudation with relatively mild pancreatic changes on follow-up CT, when accompanied by thrombocytopenia and renal dysfunction, should prompt clinicians to broaden the differential beyond pancreatic pathology.Attributing the initial retroperitoneal exudation and abdominopelvic effusion to severe acute pancreatitis follows a conventional diagnostic pathway, given that such radiological findings are well-recognized features of this condition. However, the subsequent constellation of profound thrombocytopenia, progressive renal impairment, and urinary abnormalities extended beyond the typical scope of pancreatic pathology and prompted re-evaluation of the initial diagnostic assumption (9). This scenario illustrates a classic diagnostic pitfall, where an initially plausible diagnosis supported by compelling imaging can lead to anchoring bias that delays consideration of alternative etiologies with similar radiological features. Indeed, various infections mimic the clinical and radiological presentation of acute pancreatitis, including viral pathogens that also cause systemic thrombocytopenia and renal dysfunction (16, 17); beyond pancreatitis, hantavirus infection can mimic other acute abdominal emergencies such as acute appendicitis (18, 19). The absence of typical inciting factors—such as gallstones(serum triglyceride level serial data now available in Table 2, maximal triglyceride 3.90 mmol/L, not fulfilling criteria for hypertriglyceridemic-induced pancreatitis)or hypertriglyceridemia—and the lack of significant pancreatic enzyme elevation further challenged the primary diagnosis (9).Table 2Dynamic changes of main laboratory indicators and corresponding normal reference ranges during hospitalization (*revised table: newly-added items: amylase, lipase, triglyceride, urea, creatinine, sodium, potassium, hemoglobin).Laboratory ParameterNormal Reference RangeDay1 (Admission)Day2Day4Day6Day9Day12Leucocytes (109/L)4.0–10.013.2912.8813.7610.578.18–hsCRP (mg/L)0.0–1.0–19.123.320.26.02.1Neutrophils (%)50.0–70.049.438.455.460.759.8–Lymphocyte (%)20.0–40.039.046.928.827.427.2–Monocyte percentage (%)3.0–10.011.414.315.010.411.210.7ALT (U/L)5–40187.0197.0133.081.071.059.0AST (U/L)8–40144.0–95.092.0100.079.0Platelets (10*9/L)125–35029.0100.0166.0312.0351.0358.0ALB (g/L)35.0–50.026.525.229.031.639.1–BNP (pg/mL)<125.0115.0–––––APPT(s)25.1–36.548.336.8––––Serum amylase (U/L)35–13578–82–––Serum lipase (U/L)13–6044–49–––Triglyceride (mmol/L)0.45–1.691.81–3.902.782.76–Urea (mmol/L)3.10–8.004.30–8.445.214.56–Creatinine (μmol/L)57.0–97.071.0–146.0131.0113.0–Sodium (mmol/L)137–147126.1124.6142.4143.5145.1–Potassium (mmol/L)3.5–5.53.213.103.423.403.70–Hemoglobin (g/L)130–175156.0139.0127.0127.0137.0135.0Temperature (°C)36.0–37.239.338.437.737.237.036.8hsCRP, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein; ALT, alanine aminotransferase; AST, aspartate aminotransferase; ALB, albumin; APTT, activated partial thromboplastin time; “–” indicates no test on that day.Additional note: Reticulocyte count was not obtained clinically; hemoglobin serial values are presented to evaluate for severe bone-marrow suppression. Urine sediment analysis: hematuria 2+, proteinuria1+, without granular or hyaline casts. Serial urine output was adequate, no oliguria/anuria occurred. Mixed acid-base disturbance was respiratory alkalosis with normal anion-gap.Bone-marrow suppression could not be fully excluded without reticulocyte testing; nevertheless, serial hemoglobin values did not show progressive severe anemia, which makes profound isolated bone-marrow suppression less likely in this clinical picture.The clinical profile of this patient—marked fever preceding gastntestinal symptoms, severe thrombocytopenia disproportionate to pancreatic injury, renal dysfunction with hematuria and proteinuria, and the absence of classic pancreatitis risk factors—aligns closely with previously documented patterns of hantavirus infection masquerading as pancreatic pathology. Persistent fever has consistently been identified as an early prodromal feature that predates abdominal complaints in patients with HFRS (20, 21), a sequence mirroring the chronological symptom evolution observed here. Likewise, disproportionately low platelet counts without evidence of bone marrow suppression or disseminated intravascular coagulation have been emphasized as a key hematologic clue distinguishing HFRS from primary pancreatic or biliary etiologies (10, 20). Renal involvement manifesting as proteinuria and hematuria is a hallmark of orthohantavirus infection even in atypical presentations (10). The absence of gallstones, hypertriglyceridemia, or alcohol consumption—factors accounting for most acute pancreatitis cases—has likewise been underscored in previous reports of HFRS mimicking pancreatitis (4). Radiologically, extensive retroperitoneal or peripancreatic exudation with relatively preserved pancreatic parenchyma has been documented in hantavirus-infected patients (5). Furthermore, normal or only mildly elevated pancreatic enzyme levels despite severe abdominal symptoms have been repeatedly observed in such patients, reinforcing the diagnostic challenge posed by this overlap syndrome (10).The concurrent detection of hepatitis B virus (HBV) raises the question of its potential contribution to the pancreatic injury. Viral infections are a rare but established cause of acute pancreatitis (3, 22), with a wide spectrum of pathogens implicated, including mumps virus, coxsackievirus, cytomegalovirus, and hepatitis viruses (22). Specifically, case reports and series have documented an association between hepatitis B and pancreatitis, although the pathogenic mechanism remains incompletely understood (23, 24). In a prospective study of 124 patients with acute viral hepatitis and severe abdominal pain, 7 (5.65%) were diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, one attributed to hepatitis B (24); another study from Nepal reported acute pancreatitis in 25 of 382 patients with acute viral hepatitis, though those cases were exclusively due to hepatitis E and A viruses (25). More broadly, viral infection ranks among the leading etiologies of acute pancreatitis in children (26). However, the present case diverges substantially from the typical profile of HBV-associated pancreatitis: the patient had only mild liver enzyme elevation without jaundice or other signs of acute viral hepatitis, whereas most reported HBV-related cases occurred in the setting of clinically overt acute hepatitis (24). Moreover, a study of 66 patients with acute Puumala hantavirus infection found no cases of acute pancreatitis despite frequent liver enzyme abnormalities (27). The high-copy Seoul orthohantavirus detected by mNGS, together with the characteristic sequence of fever, thrombocytopenia, renal impairment, and capillary leakage, provides a cohesive pathophysiological framework that accounts for the entire clinical course. The co-detected HBV, while a potential contributory factor, does not sufficiently explain the hematological and renal abnormalities that were the hallmark features of this case. Thus, HBV co-infection may have played at most an adjunctive role, and Seoul orthohantavirus is the principal etiological agent.Notably, inverse temporal trends between C-reactive protein and serum albumin were observed during hospitalization. Elevated CRP reflected acute-phase inflammatory response triggered by hantavirus infection, while hypoalbuminemia was multifactorial, secondary to systemic capillary leak syndrome, reduced hepatic synthesis, and protein extravasation into retroperitoneal and serous body cavities. Albumin gradually increased as capillary leakage resolved and inflammatory markers declined during clinical recovery.Regarding renal pathophysiology in HFRS: Orthohantavirus infects renal tubular endothelial cells, triggering local inflammation, increased vascular permeability, interstitial edema, and tubulo-interstitial nephritis. In our patient, urinalysis showed proteinuria and hematuria; urine sediment was negative for granular or hyaline casts. Clinical course did not develop severe renal tubular acidosis. Renal impairment was reversible, consistent with typical HFRS-associated tubulo-interstitial injury.Although mNGS offers a highly sensitive approach to pathogen detection, its output is inherently shaped by the bioinformatic pipelines and reference databases employed during analysis, which can influence the final microbial interpretation (8, 28). Its performance is not uniformly superior: targeted multiplex amplification methods have shown better overall sensitivity than mNGS for detecting respiratory viruses (29), and mNGS sensitivity can be lower for specific organisms, such as a combined sensitivity of 0.69 for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex detection in a meta-analysis (30) and reduced diagnostic accuracy for fungal infections in immunocompromised patients with suspected pneumonia (31). Moreover, the high sensitivity of mNGS may detect multiple organisms simultaneously, complicating the differentiation between true pathogens and innocent bystanders or contaminants (29). Therefore, although mNGS provides an unbiased and rapid survey of potential pathogens, its results should be interpreted al…

full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionThis case highlights a diagnostically challenging presentation in which Seoul orthohantavirus infection clinically and radiologically mimicked severe acute pancreatitis, underscoring the need to consider HFRS in the differential diagnosis of unexplained pancreatitis-like presentations (1). Acute pancreatitis is a recognized but rare complication of HFRS (2, 6), and its distinction from hantavirus-induced pancreatic involvement is notoriously difficult because of overlapping clinical and imaging features (9). The present case further illustrates that peripancreatic exudation and retroperitoneal fluid—hallmark findings of severe acute pancreatitis—can also result from the profound systemic capillary leakage and retroperitoneal edema characteristic of hantavirus infection (4, 5). In this context, marked thrombocytopenia, renal impairment with hematuria and proteinuria, and the absence of typical pancreatitis risk factors constituted pivotal clues that prompted consideration of an alternative etiology (9). Moreover, the normal pancreatic enzyme levels observed here demonstrate that biochemical markers alone cannot reliably exclude HFRS in suspected pancreatitis (10).It should be acknowledged that severe acute pancreatitis itself may produce thrombocytopenia and renal dysfunction secondary to systemic inflammation. However, several features argued against primary acute pancreatitis in this patient: thrombocytopenia was already present at initial presentation as a critical-value finding before any expected inflammatory peak of pancreatitis; renal injury was accompanied by prominent urinary findings (hematuria and proteinuria) typical for hantavirus-mediated tubular injury rather than purely pre-renal renal impairment secondary to pancreatitis-related hypovolemia; and serum amylase/lipase remained within normal reference ranges throughout admission despite extensive peripancreatic exudates on CT imaging.The dynamic imaging feature observed in this case—progressive retroperitoneal exudation on contrast-enhanced CT accompanied by relatively mild pancreatic parenchymal changes—merits particular attention in the differential diagnosis of hantavirus infection presenting with abdominal manifestations. While AP is a recognized complication of HFRS, the typical CT findings in such cases commonly include pancreatic enlargement, peripancreatic edema, and occasionally necrosis or hemorrhage (4). However, extensive retroperitoneal involvement with a relatively preserved pancreatic gland reflects the underlying pathophysiological hallmark of hantavirus infection—virus-induced increased microvascular permeability leading to fluid extravasation into the retroperitoneal space. Indeed, the retroperitoneum has been identified as a major site of vascular leak in HFRS (11), and established evidence indicates that hantavirus elicits a robust inflammatory cascade with cytokine release and endothelial dysfunction that can produce extensive retroperitoneal fluid accumulation even in the absence of true pancreatic necrosis (12, 13). Prior case reports of HFRS mimicking acute pancreatitis have generally relied on single-time-point scans and could not capture this evolving radiological signature (7). Recognition of this distinctive pattern is of substantial practical importance, particularly in endemic regions (14, 15). From a clinical standpoint, progressive retroperitoneal exudation with relatively mild pancreatic changes on follow-up CT, when accompanied by thrombocytopenia and renal dysfunction, should prompt clinicians to broaden the differential beyond pancreatic pathology.Attributing the initial retroperitoneal exudation and abdominopelvic effusion to severe acute pancreatitis follows a conventional diagnostic pathway, given that such radiological findings are well-recognized features of this condition. However, the subsequent constellation of profound thrombocytopenia, progressive renal impairment, and urinary abnormalities extended beyond the typical scope of pancreatic pathology and prompted re-evaluation of the initial diagnostic assumption (9). This scenario illustrates a classic diagnostic pitfall, where an initially plausible diagnosis supported by compelling imaging can lead to anchoring bias that delays consideration of alternative etiologies with similar radiological features. Indeed, various infections mimic the clinical and radiological presentation of acute pancreatitis, including viral pathogens that also cause systemic thrombocytopenia and renal dysfunction (16, 17); beyond pancreatitis, hantavirus infection can mimic other acute abdominal emergencies such as acute appendicitis (18, 19). The absence of typical inciting factors—such as gallstones(serum triglyceride level serial data now available in Table 2, maximal triglyceride 3.90 mmol/L, not fulfilling criteria for hypertriglyceridemic-induced pancreatitis)or hypertriglyceridemia—and the lack of significant pancreatic enzyme elevation further challenged the primary diagnosis (9).Table 2Dynamic changes of main laboratory indicators and corresponding normal reference ranges during hospitalization (*revised table: newly-added items: amylase, lipase, triglyceride, urea, creatinine, sodium, potassium, hemoglobin).Laboratory ParameterNormal Reference RangeDay1 (Admission)Day2Day4Day6Day9Day12Leucocytes (109/L)4.0–10.013.2912.8813.7610.578.18–hsCRP (mg/L)0.0–1.0–19.123.320.26.02.1Neutrophils (%)50.0–70.049.438.455.460.759.8–Lymphocyte (%)20.0–40.039.046.928.827.427.2–Monocyte percentage (%)3.0–10.011.414.315.010.411.210.7ALT (U/L)5–40187.0197.0133.081.071.059.0AST (U/L)8–40144.0–95.092.0100.079.0Platelets (10*9/L)125–35029.0100.0166.0312.0351.0358.0ALB (g/L)35.0–50.026.525.229.031.639.1–BNP (pg/mL)<125.0115.0–––––APPT(s)25.1–36.548.336.8––––Serum amylase (U/L)35–13578–82–––Serum lipase (U/L)13–6044–49–––Triglyceride (mmol/L)0.45–1.691.81–3.902.782.76–Urea (mmol/L)3.10–8.004.30–8.445.214.56–Creatinine (μmol/L)57.0–97.071.0–146.0131.0113.0–Sodium (mmol/L)137–147126.1124.6142.4143.5145.1–Potassium (mmol/L)3.5–5.53.213.103.423.403.70–Hemoglobin (g/L)130–175156.0139.0127.0127.0137.0135.0Temperature (°C)36.0–37.239.338.437.737.237.036.8hsCRP, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein; ALT, alanine aminotransferase; AST, aspartate aminotransferase; ALB, albumin; APTT, activated partial thromboplastin time; “–” indicates no test on that day.Additional note: Reticulocyte count was not obtained clinically; hemoglobin serial values are presented to evaluate for severe bone-marrow suppression. full_text_sections.other: IntroductionCase presentation and clinical dataA 33-year-old man presented with one week of recurrent fever, vomiting, and watery diarrhea. He had no history of gallstones, hypertriglyceridemia, alcohol abuse, or other recognized risk factors for acute pancreatitis. Although viral gastroenteritis could explain fever, vomiting and watery diarrhea, the presence of epigastric tenderness on physical examination together with marked peripancreatic-perirenal exudates identified on initial abdominal CT raised strong clinical suspicion for severe acute pancreatitis. Initial non-contrast abdominal CT showed peripancreatic and perirenal haziness, renal fascial thickening, and small-volume abdominopelvic effusion with mild pancreatic swelling, findings highly suggestive of severe acute pancreatitis (Figure 1).Figure 1Serial axial abdominal computed tomography (CT) images of Seoul orthohantavirus-associated capillary-leak syndrome mimicking severe acute pancreatitis. (A, C) Non-contrast abdominal CT acquired on hospital day 1 (admission). White arrows indicate the pancreas, peripancreatic fat-stranding inflammatory exudates, and thickened bilateral prerenal fascia with perirenal exudates. These radiological features initially raised high clinical suspicion for severe acute pancreatitis. (B, D) Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT acquired on hospital day 2. Compared with hospital day 1 non-contrast CT, retroperitoneal, peripancreatic and perirenal exudates are obviously progressive. After contrast administration, the pancreatic parenchyma shows no definite necrosis or large-scale parenchymal destruction.Four pairs of abdominal CT scans labeled A through D, with each pair showing Day 1 and Day 2 images, display a specific region indicated by arrows. Visible differences exist between the days, suggesting evaluation of disease progression or treatment effect.Initial supportive measures for suspected acute pancreatitis were implemented, including intravenous proton-pump inhibitor, octreotide infusion, empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics, and volume resuscitation. Of note, severe thrombocytopenia (nadir 29 × 109/L) was already documented on admission rather than developing during hospitalization. However, the patient demonstrated progressive renal impairment, hematuria, and proteinuria, without biochemical elevation of pancreatic enzymes.Two abdominal CT examinations were performed: a non-contrast CT on hospital day 1 (admission), followed by contrast-enhanced abdominal CT on hospital day 2. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed progressive retroperitoneal exudation accompanied by newly developed bilateral pleural effusion and splenomegaly.Routine work-up for undifferentiated fever was sent before mNGS testing, including bacterial blood cultures, stool culture, and a respiratory-borne viral screening panel, all of which returned negative results. Thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) laboratory screening was not performed because clinical suspicion for TMA was low: the patient lacked schistocytes on peripheral blood smear, had no severe neurologic manifestations, and mNGS rapidly identified Seoul orthohantavirus as the causative pathogen.Whole-blood mNGS detected high-copy Seoul orthohantavirus, with concurrent hepatitis B virus (HBV) and no bacterial or fungal pathogens. Hepatoprotective therapy consisted of intravenous reduced glutathione and magnesium isoglycyrrhizinate. Due to persistent vomiting, abdominal distension, and unstable clinical status precluding oral feeding, the patient was kept nil per os (NPO) at admission, not as a standard mandatory intervention for suspected acute pancreatitis. Enteral nutrition was gradually initiated once abdominal symptoms improved. After supportive care, intravenous immunoglobulin, albumin supplementation, hepatoprotective therapy, and electrolyte correction, the patient recovered fully; pre-discharge ultrasound showed normal pancreatic morphology (Figure 2).Figure 2Pre-discharge abdominal ultrasound obtained on hospital day 12 (at discharge). (A) Color-Doppler ultrasound view of upper abdomen. (B) Grayscale two-dimensional ultrasound image. White arrows mark the pancreatic gland. The pancreas presents normal parenchymal echotexture, without swelling, enlargement or surrounding fluid-collection, confirming complete resolution of previous retro-peritoneal inflammatory exudative lesions.Panel A displays a color Doppler abdominal ultrasound of the upper abdomen with a white arrow indicating the pancreatic gland and regions of color denoting blood flow. Panel B shows a grayscale two-dimensional ultrasound image of the same region with a white arrow pointing to the pancreas, revealing homogeneous echotexture without swelling, enlargement, or fluid collection.Laboratory and imaging findingsInitial laboratory investigations showed a mixed acid-base disturbance, characterized by respiratory alkalosis with normal anion-gap (AnGap 2-10 mmol/L),hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and liver function injury. The most striking abnormality was profound thrombocytopenia (29 × 109/L); urinalysis revealed hematuria and proteinuria.Table 2 was revised to add serum amylase, lipase, serum triglyceride, serum urea, serum creatinine, sodium, potassium, hemoglobin values. Reticulocyte count was not tested in clinical practice; hemoglobin levels over serial time-points are presented to evaluate for bone-marrow suppression. Urine sediment examination did not demonstrate granular or hyaline casts. Serial urine output was prospectively recorded as part of intensive care monitoring; overall urine output remained adequate throughout hospitalization without anuria or oliguric renal failure. Mild anemia was observed (minimum hemoglobin 127 g/L).Serial changes in leukocytes, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, neutrophil and lymphocyte percentages, transaminases, platelets, albumin, and coagulation parameters are summarized in Table 2. The dynamic clinical, laboratory, imaging, and management course across hospitalization is summarized in the diagnostic timeline (Table 1).Table 1Diagnostic timeline.Time pointClinical manifestationsKey laboratory findingsImaging & pathogen testClinical management & decision-makingOne week before admissionLow-grade intermittent fever, lumbago; elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 入院时他已出现严重血小板减少症(最低值 29 × 109/L)、进行性肾功能损害、血尿和蛋白尿,但没有典型的胰腺炎危险因素或胰酶升高。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 讨论该病例强调了一种诊断上具有挑战性的表现,其中首尔正汉坦病毒感染在临床和放射学上与严重急性胰腺炎相似,强调在鉴别不明原因的胰腺炎样表现的 诊断 时需要考虑 HFRS (1)。
elements_zh.methods: 全血宏基因组下一代测序(mNGS)检测到高拷贝首尔正汉坦病毒,同时存在乙型肝炎病毒。
elements_zh.main_results: 最初的腹部平扫 CT 显示胰周和肾周混浊、肾筋膜增厚、少量腹盆腔积液并伴有轻度胰腺肿胀,这些结果高度提示重症急性胰腺炎(图 1)。图 1 首尔正汉坦病毒相关毛细血管渗漏综合征的串行轴向腹部计算机断层扫描 (CT) 图像,类似于重症急性胰腺炎。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 通过支持治疗、静脉注射免疫球蛋白和有症状的 治疗,患者完全康复;出院前超声显示胰腺形态正常。结论首尔正汉坦病毒感染在临床和影像学上与重症急性胰腺炎非常相似。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 网织红细胞计数未在临床实践中进行测试;提供连续时间点的血红蛋白水平以评估骨髓抑制。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 虽然病毒性胃肠炎可以解释发热、呕吐和水样腹泻,但体检时出现上腹压痛,加上初次腹部 CT 发现明显的胰周-肾周渗出物,引起了临床对重症急性胰腺炎的强烈怀疑。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 入院时他已出现严重血小板减少症(最低值 29 × 109/L)、进行性肾功能损害、血尿和蛋白尿,但没有典型的胰腺炎危险因素或胰酶升高。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 讨论该病例强调了一种诊断上具有挑战性的表现,其中首尔正汉坦病毒感染在临床和放射学上与严重急性胰腺炎相似,强调在鉴别不明原因的胰腺炎样表现的 诊断 时需要考虑 HFRS (1)。
analysis_zh.methods: 全血宏基因组下一代测序(mNGS)检测到高拷贝首尔正汉坦病毒,同时存在乙型肝炎病毒。
analysis_zh.main_results: 最初的腹部平扫 CT 显示胰周和肾周混浊、肾筋膜增厚、少量腹盆腔积液并伴有轻度胰腺肿胀,这些结果高度提示重症急性胰腺炎(图 1)。图 1 首尔正汉坦病毒相关毛细血管渗漏综合征的串行轴向腹部计算机断层扫描 (CT) 图像,类似于重症急性胰腺炎。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 通过支持治疗、静脉注射免疫球蛋白和有症状的 治疗,患者完全康复;出院前超声显示胰腺形态正常。结论首尔正汉坦病毒感染在临床和影像学上与重症急性胰腺炎非常相似。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 网织红细胞计数未在临床实践中进行测试;提供连续时间点的血红蛋白水平以评估骨髓抑制。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 虽然病毒性胃肠炎可以解释发热、呕吐和水样腹泻,但体检时出现上腹压痛,加上初次腹部 CT 发现明显的胰周-肾周渗出物,引起了临床对重症急性胰腺炎的强烈怀疑。

papers.title: Immature Platelet Fraction in Viral Infections: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Background: Reticulated platelets, reported by modern hematology analyzers as the immature platelet fraction (IPF%) or the absolute immature platelet count (IPC), index thrombopoiesis and have been proposed as biomarkers in the thrombocytopenia of viral infection. Methods: This systematic review, conducted and reported following PRISMA 2020 and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261501412), examined how these parameters have been used across viral diseases. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2000 to May 2025 for observational studies of adults with viral infection reporting IPF, IPC, or reticulated platelets, and methodological robustness was appraised with the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale. Results: Twenty-two studies were included and synthesized narratively. Applications differed by pathogen: in dengue, serial IPF increases consistently preceded platelet recovery, although proposed thresholds varied; in COVID-19, higher immature platelet parameters were associated with severity and mortality but were inconsistent after adjustment. Evidence in chronic hepatitis, HIV, hantavirus, and Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever was mainly pathophysiological, and data in critically ill patients were almost confined to COVID-19. Conclusions: Clinical value appears disease- and outcome-specific: serial IPF best predicts platelet recovery in dengue, whereas prognostic use in COVID-19 remains insufficiently validated. Analytical heterogeneity and the absence of transferable thresholds currently limit clinical implementation.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 现代血液分析仪将网织血小板报告为未成熟血小板分数 (IPF%) 或绝对未成熟血小板计数 (IPC),它指示血小板生成,并已被提议作为病毒感染血小板减少症的生物标志物。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 检索了 2000 年 1 月至 2025 年 5 月期间 PubMed、Scopus 和 Cochrane 图书馆对报告 IPF、IPC 或网织血小板的病毒感染成人的观察性研究,并使用纽卡斯尔-渥太华量表评估了方法的稳健性。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 应用因病原体而异:在登革热中,尽管提出的阈值有所不同,但在血小板恢复之前,IPF 持续增加;在 COVID-19 中,较高的未成熟血小板参数与严重程度和 死亡率 相关,但调整后不一致。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 分析异质性和缺乏可转移阈值目前限制了临床实施。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 临床价值似乎针对疾病和结果:连续 IPF 最能预测登革热的血小板恢复,而在 COVID-19 中的预后用途尚未得到充分验证。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:网织血小板,由现代血液分析仪报告为未成熟血小板分数 (IPF%) 或绝对未成熟血小板计数 (IPC),可指示血小板生成,并已被提议作为病毒感染血小板减少症的生物标志物。方法:这项系统评价是在 PRISMA 2020 之后进行和报告的,并在 PROSPERO (CRD420261501412) 中注册,检查了这些参数如何在病毒性疾病中使用。检索了 2000 年 1 月至 2025 年 5 月期间 PubMed、Scopus 和 Cochrane 图书馆对报告 IPF、IPC 或网织血小板的病毒感染成人的观察性研究,并使用纽卡斯尔-渥太华量表评估了方法的稳健性。结果:纳入了 22 项研究并进行了叙述性综合。应用因病原体而异:在登革热中,尽管提出的阈值有所不同,但在血小板恢复之前,IPF 持续增加;在 COVID-19 中,较高的未成熟血小板参数与严重程度和 死亡率 相关,但调整后不一致。慢性肝炎、HIV、汉坦病毒和克里米亚-刚果出血热的证据主要是病理生理学的,危重患者的数据几乎仅限于COVID-19。结论:临床价值似乎针对疾病和结果:系列 IPF 最能预测登革热的血小板恢复,而在 COVID-19 中的预后用途尚未得到充分验证。分析异质性和缺乏可转移阈值目前限制了临床实施。

papers.title: Reverse Vaccinology Design of an Asian HLA-Targeted Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against HTNV Strain 76-118
papers.abstract: HTNV remains a cause of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, particularly in Asia, while broadly available vaccines remain limited. This study developed an Asian HLA-targeted multi-epitope vaccine candidate against HTNV strain 76-118 using reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics. RdRp, GPC, and N proteins were screened for cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL), helper T-lymphocyte (HTL), and linear B-cell epitopes using 42 representative Asian HLA alleles. Selected epitopes were evaluated for immunological and safety properties, followed by population coverage analysis, vaccine construction, immune simulation, structural modeling, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics simulation, MM-GBSA analysis, and in silico cloning. Twenty-five epitopes, comprising 10 CTL, 10 HTL, and 5 B-cell epitopes, were retained. Combined MHC class I and II predicted coverage averaged 95.15% across five regions and reached 99.29% in East Asia. Among four adjuvant-based constructs, the HBHA-containing vaccine was prioritized based on combined physicochemical and comparative immune-simulation characteristics. Docking with TLR4 yielded a predicted ΔG of −27.6 kcal mol−1, while trajectory-based MM-GBSA analysis produced a ΔGbind of −136.17 ± 3.14 kcal mol−1. Codon optimization achieved a CAI of 0.9640 and GC content of 52.27%. Collectively, these computational analyses identify the HBHA-based construct as a population-oriented HTNV vaccine candidate prioritized for subsequent experimental evaluation.

Selected epitopes were evaluated for immunological and safety properties, followed by population coverage analysis, vaccine construction, immune simulation, structural modeling, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics simulation, MM-GBSA analysis, and in silico cloning. Combined MHC class I and II predicted coverage averaged 95.15% across five regions and reached 99.29% in East Asia. Among four adjuvant-based constructs, the HBHA-containing vaccine was prioritized based on combined physicochemical and comparative immune-simulation characteristics. Docking with TLR4 yielded a predicted ΔG of −27.6 kcal mol−1, while trajectory-based MM-GBSA analysis produced a ΔGbind of −136.17 ± 3.14 kcal mol−1. Codon optimization achieved a CAI of 0.9640 and GC content of 52.27%. Collectively, these computational analyses identify the HBHA-based construct as a population-oriented HTNV vaccine candidate prioritized for subsequent experimental evaluation.
papers.abstract_zh: HTNV 仍然是 肾综合征出血热 的一个原因,特别是在亚洲,而广泛使用的 疫苗 仍然有限。本研究利用反向疫苗学和免疫信息学开发了针对 HTNV 76-118 株的亚洲 HLA 靶向多表位 疫苗 候选药物。使用 42 个代表性亚洲 HLA 等位基因筛选 RdRp、GPC 和 N 蛋白的细胞毒性 T 淋巴细胞 (CTL)、辅助 T 淋巴细胞 (HTL) 和线性 B 细胞表位。对选定表位的免疫学和安全特性进行评估,然后进行群体覆盖分析、疫苗 构建、免疫模拟、结构建模、分子对接、300 ns 分子动力学模拟、MM-GBSA 分析和计算机克隆。保留了 25 个表位,包括 10 个 CTL、10 个 HTL 和 5 个 B 细胞表位。MHC I 类和 II 类综合预测覆盖率在五个地区平均为 95.15%,在东亚达到 99.29%。在四种基于佐剂的构建体中,基于综合物理化学和比较免疫模拟特性,含有 HBHA 的 疫苗 被优先考虑。与 TLR4 对接产生的预测 ΔG 为 -27.6 kcal mol−1,而基于轨迹的 MM-GBSA 分析产生的 ΔGbind 为 -136.17 ± 3.14 kcal mol−1。密码子优化实现CAI为0.9640,GC含量为52.27%。总的来说,这些计算分析将基于 HBHA 的构建体确定为面向群体的 HTNV 疫苗 候选者,优先用于后续实验评估。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 13, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Hantavirus Neutralizing Antibodies Differ Between Historical Vaccine and Circulating Chinese Strains by November 11, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 4 mins read 0 Hantavirus Neutralizing Antibodies Differ Between Historical Vaccine and Circulating Chinese Strains Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Neutralizing antibody titers against Hantavirus differ significantly between historical vaccine strains and representative circulating epidemic strains in China, according to a comparative evaluation of convalescent patient and vaccinee sera. The investigation assessed whether viral divergence across rodent reservoirs influences the humoral immunity elicited by long-standing immunization programs. Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), caused by Hantavirus, continues to present a significant public health burden globally. In key endemic provinces throughout China, prevention efforts have relied on a bivalent inactivated vaccine formulated with Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV) strains originally isolated two decades ago. Following decades of comprehensive control measures, HFRS incidence in China has transitioned into a phase of low-level epidemic fluctuation. Nevertheless, ongoing viral transmission within wild rodent host populations can spur dynamic shifts in genetic diversity and immunogenicity, creating uncertainty regarding ongoing vaccine-induced protection and underlying pathogenic mechanisms. Discover more vaccine Find Vaccines vaccinee vaccines Vaccine To evaluate these immune responses, researchers established a serum panel comprising convalescent samples from clinical HFRS cases alongside specimens from individuals who received standardized immunization with the bivalent inactivated vaccine. Using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay-based microneutralization test (MN-ELISA), neutralizing antibody titers were measured against the HTNV vaccine strain 84FLi, the SEOV vaccine strain L99, and three representative epidemic strains representing distinct genotypes: HTNV strain SX26 and SEOV strains LN03 and FJ-17. Hantavirus-neutralizing antibodies were successfully detected across all tested serum samples. Among the 48 evaluated HFRS patients, laboratory identification categorized 47.92 percent (23 of 48) as HTNV infections, 27.08 percent (13 of 48) as SEOV infections, and 25 percent (12 of 48) as untypable cases. Titers against vaccine strains and circulating epidemic strains exhibited pronounced divergence. news.content: Mirage News Mirage News Mirage News Science 13 Nov 2026 6:56 am AEDT Date Time Discover more Read Daily News news News Published on An international consortium including UNIGE and HUG has clarified the origin and mode of transmission of the Andes virus, which spread aboard a cruise ship in spring 2026. High-security P4 laboratory at Geneva University Hospitals (HUG), specialising in the analysis and handling of the most dangerous pathogens. © Nicolas Schopfer - HUG An international collaboration involving the University of Geneva (UNIGE) and the Geneva University Hospitals (HUG) has confirmed that the hantavirus outbreak aboard the M/V Hondius in April 2026 stemmed from an initial infection acquired on land, followed by person-to-person transmission on board. Genetic analyses show that the virus belongs to a natural lineage of the Andes virus circulating in Argentine Patagonia. Published in Science, these findings highlights the vital role of scientific cooperation in responding to global health emergencies. In April 2026, an outbreak of severe respiratory infections, presenting as hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), was detected aboard the cruise ship M/V Hondius, which had left Ushuaia, Argentina, on 1 April. Analyses conducted by the UNIGE/HUG Geneva Centre for Emerging Viral Diseases , a WHO Collaborating Centre, identified the virus as belonging to the Andes strain. In total, thirteen passengers were affected, three of whom died. Two questions remained unanswered: how did the virus spread on board, and where did the infection originate? "Hantaviruses are usually transmitted by inhaling dust contaminated with the secretions of wild rodents. The Andes virus, however, has the rare ability to also pass directly from person to person through close, prolonged contact," explains Isabella Eckerle, Director of the UNIGE/HUG Centre, which also hosts the Swiss Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH) reference lab for emerging viral diseases. Discover more National News Updates World News Feed Business News Analysis This extraordinary international effort underlines how essential it is to invest in national capacities and international scientific networks before a crisis occurs. Tracing the virus's path To gain further insights, an international collaboration in which Isabella Eckerle is actively involved carried out an epidemiological and genetic investigation. The scientists initially observed that the first case was reported on 3 April, shortly after departure from Ushuaia. By contrast, case "13" developed symptoms on 31 May 2026, 60 days after leaving Argentina. This far exceeds the maximum known incubation period for initial infection from rodents, estimated at six weeks. This part of the research further documented close and prolonged contact between this patient and another confirmed case, case "10". The team then sequenced the virus genome, determining the order of the elements that make up its genetic material, in ten of the thirteen affected individuals. They found that the genetic material was highly similar across all individuals. "The sequence of symptom onset, the genomic data, and the patterns of close contact all point to an initial introduction of the virus from a rodent to a passenger, followed by secondary person-to-person transmission on board the ship," says Isabella Eckerle, citing the study's conclusions. Discover more Technology News Reports Buy Maps Explore History A known virus The analysis also shows that virus from the cruise ship is genetically very close to natural strains of the Andes virus circulating in Argentine Patagonia. This rules out rumours of an artificial or reassorted virus, or one that had undergone abnormal mutations. The international consortium also published a second article in Science , tracing the historical lineage of the virus strain in Patagonia. This work is the result of extensive international collaboration, particularly through the independent comparison of results between laboratories in several countries (France, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Spain, Canada, Senegal, and South Africa). This strengthened the robustness and reliability of the genomic analyses used to trace the transmission pathway on board. "This extraordinary international effort shows what we can achieve by working together, across institutions and borders. It underlines how essential it is to invest in national capacities and international scientific networks before a crisis occurs," concludes Isabella Eckerle.
